newsitem.title: JAPAN: Maruha to abandon shipping business on March 31.
newsitem.headline: Maruha to abandon shipping business on March 31.

text.p: Maruha Corp said on Tuesday that it would abandon its shipping business on March 31, but said the move would not affect its current earnings forecast for the year to that date.

Most of Maruha's sales currently come from its marine food products business, including production and sales of canned and frozen food, but it deals with other businesses, including shipping operations.

"We have been making cost-cutting efforts in hopes of continuing the shipping business in a sluggish market but we decided that our efforts would not be sufficient to deal with the severe business environment," Maruha said in a statement.
"We decided to withdraw from the shipping business and to liquidate our shipping subsidiary," it said.
Maruha said it expected an extraordinary loss of 4.1 billion yen to be included in its earnings for 1996/97 but that it planned to offset the special loss by selling assets.
Maruha said in November that it expected to post parent current profit of four billion yen in 1996/97, against a profit of 2.95 billion yen in the previous year.
It expected a net profit of 1.5 billion yen in 1996/97, up from 856 million yen in 1995/96.
